title: Redwood - NovaEdge Marketplace Integration Tech Sync
meeting_header: 2026-11-30 15:00 PST — 48 mins — Attendees: Redwood (Matt, Priya, Diego) + NovaEdge (Liam, Janelle, Sara, Ben). Recording enabled.
summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for Redwood Private on NovaEdge marketplace, and joint solution validation steps. Main concerns: VPC connectivity, KMS/HSM support, certs for marketplace packaging, and performance benchmarking. Agreed next steps include sharing listing template, reference arch diagram, and scheduling a pilot benchmark week.
topics: KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in transit
transcript: 00:00 Matt King: Hey everybody, thanks for joining — can you all hear me okay?
00:05 Liam O'Connor: Yeah, loud and clear. Thanks Matt. We're eager to get the marketplace listing, yeah.
00:12 Priya Shah: Great. I can share my screen in a sec — quick agenda: listing fields, reference arch for Private/VPC, certs/KMS, and then a pilot/benchmark plan.
00:20 Sara Lee: That works. We're mainly worried about the onboarding flow for our customers — they want one-click marketplace install but also need to ensure keys never leave our KMS.

00:30 Matt King: Totally, that's a common ask. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations — we do not persist plaintext keys in our control plane, and we can do key wrapping, etc. we'll include the KMS support details in the marketplace doc.
00:45 Ben T.: Quick note — NovaEdge has its own CMP and we prefer SAML SSO for the console. Does Redwood support SSO via SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?

00:55 Priya Shah: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning and we can wire RBAC to your identity provider. small caveat: the installer for Private needs an admin user initially but that's a one-time bootstrap; we can document the steps.
01:10 Janelle Park: On the packaging side — marketplace requires a reference arch diagram, a security checklist, and a brief runbook for upgrades. Do you have a canonical ref-arch we can adapt?

01:22 Diego Ramos: We do. I'll send a base reference architecture for Redwood Private on cloud marketplaces — includes VPC peering patterns, transit gateway options, and an on-prem variant. We'll annotate where KV cache and batchers live, and the minimal GPU footprint for small pilots.
01:38 Liam O'Connor: When you say 'KV cache' sometimes it shows up as 'K V cache' in docs — ok cool. Also we need to quantify latency impact of prefix caching vs not.

01:48 Priya Shah: Yes, good call. For the benchmarks we'll provide two workload profiles — low-latency gen and high-throughput batched embeddings — and show token p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also include fallback to lighter quantized models for cost-sensitive routes.
02:05 Sara Lee: We're going to run the pilot in our staging VPC first. How much access do you need? Do you prefer a peered VPC or a managed VPN?

02:15 Matt King: Peered VPC is cleaner for performance, but we can support a site-to-site VPN if you need to avoid direct peering. For the initial benchmark peering is preferred to reduce variability.
02:25 Ben T.: And network egress costs — if Redwood sends telemetry to your control plane, are those endpoints configurable?

02:33 Priya Shah: Telemetry endpoints are configurable; customers can opt to route telemetry to a customer-owned collector or disable telemetry collection for compliance. We'll capture that in the security checklist.
02:46 Janelle Park: Marketplace listing metadata — we need the short description, tags, and the deploy options. Redwood, can you provide the required metadata fields?

02:55 Diego Ramos: Yes, marketplace template — I'll fill in the sections: product summary, supported deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private), minimum infra, IAM requirements, and a short demo video link. We'll send the filled template by EOD tomorrow.
03:10 Liam O'Connor: What's the typical turnaround for security review? Our procurement expects SOC2 Type II evidence and a penetration test report.

03:18 Matt King: For SOC 2 we can share the letter; penetration test summary is available — for Private deployments we also provide configuration hardening docs. We'll drop the security pack into the shared folder.

03:28 Sara Lee: Awesome. On the reference arch — our infra teams insist on KMS provenence: we need to ensure CMKs stay in our account and are never exported. Does Redwood support CMKs in customer account?

03:39 Priya Shah: Yes, we support customer-managed CMKs — keys stay in your account; we do key wrapping to encrypt any tokens we need to store. We'll list supported KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and AWS CloudHSM for HSM-backed keys).
03:52 Ben T.: Any specific cert requirements for marketplace packaging? We have an internal CA, is mutual TLS supported?

03:58 Diego Ramos: Mutual TLS is supported for service-to-service communications; our installer can be configured with customer certs. For marketplace, we include a step-by-step for cert insertion and rotation cadence recommendations.
04:10 Janelle Park: Regarding the listing, marketplace wants a logo and a 1-minute demo video. We'll coordinate on assets — who owns the demo recording?
04:17 Matt King: Redwood can produce a short demo; if NovaEdge prefers a co-branded video, we can jointly record a quick walkthrough. We'll also provide a short script for the demo.
04:28 Liam O'Connor: For benchmarking — can Redwood run a self-hosted benchmark harness inside our staging to measure p95/p99? Or do you want us to run the tests locally and share logs?

04:37 Priya Shah: We recommend running a joint benchmark: Redwood SE will run the harness with your team in staging so we can control variables and collect KV cache hit/miss rates. We'll need SSH or admin console access per the runbook.
04:52 Sara Lee: Ok, scheduling — we're available next week for a 3-day benchmark window, earliest Mon-Tues. That should be enough for the initial profiles.
05:00 Matt King: Great, we'll tentatively target Monday 12/7 for the kickoff and send a calendar invite after this call.
05:07 Ben T.: Small sniff — if the marketplace requires automated upgrades, how does Redwood handle rolling updates for Private installs?

05:14 Priya Shah: For Private we support canary and rolling upgrades controlled by the customer; the marketplace listing will include upgrade options and an ops checklist. We don't auto-upgrade without the customer's consent.
05:25 Janelle Park: Any blockers on your side for the initial listing?

05:28 Diego Ramos: No blockers — deliverables from Redwood: filled marketplace template, ref-arch diagram (drawn), security pack, demo script, and a pilot benchmark plan. Deliverables from NovaEdge: logo, billing/marketplace contact, and staging VPC access window.

05:45 Liam O'Connor: We'll get the logo and contacts by Thursday. One ask — can you include a cost-estimate worksheet for 10k requests/day and 100k embeddings/month? Procurement wants rough pricing to go to internal stakeholders.
05:58 Matt King: Yes, I'll attach a conservative estimate and also include dedicated vs hosted cost comparatives. We'll include unit economics assumptions (token sizes, batching efficiency).
06:10 Sara Lee: On SLAs — does Redwood provide uptime SLAs for Private installs or is that only for Dedicated?

06:17 Priya Shah: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime. For Private we provide operational support SLAs depending on the enterprise support tier; we can add an addendum for marketplace customers on a case-by-case basis.
06:27 Ben T.: One technical detail — latency sensitive inference uses KV cache warm-up. How do you recommend pre-warming caches across replicas?
06:35 Diego Ramos: We usually preload common prefixes and maintain a warm cache via scheduled prefetch jobs. We'll include a recommended prewarm plan and scripts in the runbook.
06:48 Liam O'Connor: Does the prewarm require special API keys? We want to limit key scope.
06:53 Priya Shah: Prefetch jobs can be executed with a scoped service account limited to cache operations; we'll document the minimal IAM policy.
07:02 Janelle Park: Any mentions of competitors we should avoid in the marketplace blurb?
07:06 Matt King: Best to keep it neutral. Internally folks mentioned Anthro, CloudAI, but we won't call them out in the listing.
07:15 Sara Lee: For observability, what dashboards will be available? We need token-level billing, per-model latency, and error traces.

07:23 Diego Ramos: Redwood Console provides per-route latency/cost breakdowns, tracing hooks, and error analysis. We'll include screenshots in the listing pack — some images will be redacted but we'll provide representative dashboards.
07:35 Ben T.: For compliance, do you provide audit logs and retention controls?
07:39 Priya Shah: Yes, audit logs with retention configurable — we can export to your SIEM. We'll include the retention options and recommended settings.
07:48 Liam O'Connor: Ok, I think that's the bulk. Can we run through explicit next steps?

07:52 Matt King: Sure. Redwood deliverables: 1) Completed marketplace template (Diego) by EOD tomorrow; 2) Reference architecture diagram and runbook (Diego/Priya) by Friday; 3) Security pack with SOC2 letter and penetration summary (Matt) within 48 hours; 4) Demo script and optional co-branded recording plan (Matt) by next Tue; 5) Benchmark plan and calendar invite for 12/7 (Priya).

08:20 Janelle Park: NovaEdge deliverables: 1) Logo and marketplace contact info by Thursday; 2) Staging VPC access window and ops contact for 12/7 by next Mon; 3) Internal pricing approver contact (procurement) — we'll share that by Friday.
08:37 Liam O'Connor: One more Q — for billing through the marketplace, do you require a separate contract or can it be transacted directly through NovaEdge marketplace?
08:45 Matt King: We support marketplace billing flows; contract terms can be templated via the marketplace. We'll send sample T&Cs in the listing packet.
08:55 Sara Lee: Thanks everyone. Anything else?
08:58 Matt King: Nothing else from Redwood. We'll follow up with a shared folder link and the invite. Thanks all.
09:03 Meeting end
